source.author: stat
source.text: summa crepant auro, Tyrioque attollitur ostro molle supercilium, teretes hoc undique gemmae irradiant, medio Linus intertextus acantho letiferique canes: opus admirabile semper oderat atque oculos flectebat ab omine mater, arma etiam et veterum exuvias circumdat avorum gloria mixta malis afflictaeque ambitus aulae, ceu grande exsequiis onus atque immensa ferantur membra rogo, sed cassa tamen sterilisque dolentes fama iuvat, parvique augescunt funere manes, inde ingens lacrimis honor et miseranda voluptas, muneraque in cineres annis graviora feruntur namque illi et pharetras brevioraque tela dicarat festinus voti pater insontesque sagittas; iam tunc et nota stabuli de gente probatos in nomen pascebat equos cinctusque sonantes armaque maiores exspectatura lacertos.
source.text_original: summa crepant auro, Tyrioque attollitur ostro / molle supercilium, teretes hoc undique gemmae / irradiant, medio Linus intertextus acantho / letiferique canes: opus admirabile semper / oderat atque oculos flectebat ab omine mater, / arma etiam et veterum exuvias circumdat avorum / gloria mixta malis afflictaeque ambitus aulae, / ceu grande exsequiis onus atque immensa ferantur / membra rogo, sed cassa tamen sterilisque dolentes / fama iuvat, parvique augescunt funere manes, / inde ingens lacrimis honor et miseranda voluptas, / muneraque in cineres annis graviora feruntur — / namque illi et pharetras brevioraque tela dicarat / festinus voti pater insontesque sagittas; / iam tunc et nota stabuli de gente probatos / in nomen pascebat equos — cinctusque sonantes / armaque maiores exspectatura lacertos.
source.text_english: The topmost parts creak with gold, and a soft brow rises with Tyrian purple; smooth gems shine all around it, and in the middle, entwined acanthus and deadly hounds: she had always hated the wondrous work and turned her eyes away from the omen. Even weapons and the spoils of their ancestors are hung about it, glory mingled with misfortune, the court’s pageantry afflicting the troubled palace, as though great weight and vast limbs were being borne to burial pyre; yet vain and barren fame still gives comfort to the grieving, and the spirits grow great through the funeral rites of the little ones. From this comes a vast honor in tears and a pitiable delight, and gifts are carried to the ashes, heavier with the years. For for him too the eager father had dedicated quivers and shorter shafts, and innocent arrows as a vow; even then he was feeding in his name the horses, approved from the well-known stock of the stable, and the girded arms and ringing weapons that awaited his grown limbs.

reuse.text: at quibus arvorum studiumque insontis aratri, hos stimulant magnaque ratem per lustra viasque visi laude canunt manifesto in lumine Fauni silvarumque deae atque elatis cornibus Amnes.
reuse.text_original: at quibus arvorum studiumque insontis aratri, / hos stimulant magnaque ratem per lustra viasque / visi laude canunt manifesto in lumine Fauni / silvarumque deae atque elatis cornibus Amnes.
reuse.text_english: But those in whom there is a passion for the fields and for the guiltless plough, these are spurred on; and, as they are seen, they sing of the raft through the years and roads with great praise, in clear light, along with Fauni, the goddesses of the woods, and the Rivers with uplifted horns.
